issues.issue: Was Mr. Wong's guilty plea informed, given he did not know of the immigration consequences?
issues.applicant_position: Wong did not know his plea carried immigration consequences, so the plea was uninformed.
issues.result_quote: His guilty plea was therefore uninformed.

issues.issue: What must an accused show to withdraw an uninformed plea: subjective prejudice or a modified objective test?
issues.result_quote: In our view, the accused should be required to establish subjective prejudice.

issues.issue: Must an accused who seeks to withdraw a plea show a viable defence or route to acquittal?
issues.applicant_position: Accused need not show a viable defence to withdraw an uninformed plea on procedural grounds.
issues.result_quote: the accused need not show a viable defence to the charge in order to withdraw a plea on procedural grounds

issues.issue: Does the ineffective assistance of counsel framework apply to withdrawing an uninformed plea?
issues.applicant_position: Framed as an ineffective assistance of trial counsel claim in the Court of Appeal.
issues.result_quote: the ineffective assistance of counsel framework has no relevance to this case

issues.issue: Has Wong shown prejudice, i.e. that he would have proceeded differently had he been informed?
issues.applicant_position: His main concern was avoiding deportation, so he would have proceeded differently; his submissions suggest this.
issues.result_quote: he has not established prejudice giving rise to a miscarriage of justice
